paper_title: Improving Process Compatibility of Multilayer Organic Fiber Photodetectors by Combining Coaxial Thermal Evaporation with Dip-Coating
source_file: /home/wzfeng/MySearch/PhotoRag/MD/Adv Materials Technologies - 2024 - Wu - Improving Process Compatibility of Multilayer Organic Fiber Photodetectors by/auto/Adv Materials Technologies - 2024 - Wu - Improving Process Compatibility of Multilayer Organic Fiber Photodetectors by.md

knowledge_points.content: The organic fiber photodetector (OFPD) utilizes a five-layer coaxial diode structure consisting of Zn (core wire) / ZnO (ETL) / PBDB-T:ITIC-Th (active layer) / MoO3 (HTL) / PEDOT:PSS (transparent electrode).
knowledge_points.evidence: Herein, a diode-type five-layer OFPD with Zn/ZnO/PBDB-T:ITIC-Th, MoO3/PEDOT:PSS structure is prepared by combining thermal evaporation with a successive dip-coating method.

knowledge_points.content: A hybrid fabrication strategy is employed where the ZnO, organic photosensitive layer, and PEDOT:PSS are deposited via dip-coating, while the MoO3 layer is deposited using a specialized fiber-compatible thermal evaporation technique involving fiber rotation.
knowledge_points.evidence: the uniform coaxial MoO3 interfacial layer is processed by the proposed fiber-compatible thermal evaporation technique, while the other functional layers are enabled by the solution-based dip-coating method... the fiber substrate was rotated around an axis by the reversing equipment.

knowledge_points.content: At a bias of -0.5 V, the optimized OFPD achieves a dark current density of 8.46 × 10^-8 A cm^-2 and a responsivity of 86.4 mA W^-1 at a wavelength of 760 nm.
knowledge_points.evidence: At the bias of -0.5 V, the optimized OFPD exhibits a dark current density of 8.46 × 10^-8 A cm^-2, a responsivity of 86.4 mA W^-1 (@ 760 nm)

knowledge_points.content: The OFPD exhibits a specific detectivity (D*) exceeding 10^11 Jones across the visible spectrum range of 400 to 760 nm.
knowledge_points.evidence: and a specific detectivity of over 10^11 Jones in the visible range of 400-760 nm.

knowledge_points.content: The device demonstrates a fast temporal response with a rise time of 0.44 ms and a fall time of 0.14 ms at 0 V bias under 650 nm laser pulse excitation.
knowledge_points.evidence: the device displays a fast response speed of 0.44 and 0.14 ms for rise and fall time... the response time of the device was tested at 0 V bias using a 650 nm laser pulse.

knowledge_points.content: The thickness of the MoO3 hole transport layer significantly influences the dark current; an optimal thickness of 80 nm (measured by planar crystal oscillator) provides the lowest dark current density of 8.46 × 10^-8 A cm^-2 by effectively acting as an electron blocking layer.
knowledge_points.evidence: When the MoO3 film thickness was 20 nm the dark current of the device rose fast... When the film thickness was 80 nm the Jd was the lowest (8.46 × 10^-8 A cm^-2).

knowledge_points.content: Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) analysis on the curved fiber surface shows that the root-mean-square (RMS) roughness increases from the ZnO layer (0.84 nm) to the active layer (1.44 nm), and further to the MoO3 layer (2.5 nm).
knowledge_points.evidence: the surface root-mean-square (RMS) roughness of the ZnO layer is 0.84 nm... The RMS roughness of the PBDB-T:ITIC-Th organic photosensitive layer is 1.44 nm... After depositing a certain amount of MoO3 the RMS roughness is 2.5 nm

knowledge_points.content: The coaxial design of the fiber photodetector enables 360-degree full-angle light detection with a response uniformity where the ratio between minimum and maximum response points exceeds 80%.
knowledge_points.evidence: Figure 4a demonstrates that the ratio between the minimum and maximum response points was over 80%, indicating the device had excellent uniformity... suitable for detecting light from all angles.

knowledge_points.content: The OFPD maintains 86% of its initial photocurrent after 1000 bending cycles at a 45-degree angle, while the dark current increases by only 8% over the same period.
knowledge_points.evidence: during the 1000 times of bending, the photocurrent did not drop obviously (maintaining 86% of the initial value). The dark current increased slightly... after 1000 times, it increased by 8% compared with the initial value.

knowledge_points.content: To prevent electrical short-circuiting during the final dip-coating of the PEDOT:PSS electrode, the fiber ends are insulated using Polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS).
knowledge_points.evidence: In order to prevent the short circuit, polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS from Dow Corning) was added dropwise to the end of the device before dip-coating the external electrodes

knowledge_points.content: The active layer utilizes a bulk heterojunction (BHJ) blend of the polymer donor PBDB-T and the small molecule acceptor ITIC-Th in a 1:1 mass ratio, chosen for their complementary absorption in the visible spectrum.
knowledge_points.evidence: Organic photosensitive layer solution: PBDB-T and ITIC-Th with a mass ratio of 1:1 were dissolved in chlorobenzene... Due to the strong and complementary absorption of the electron donor and acceptor materials in the visible light band... PBDB-T:ITIC-Th is a common combination

knowledge_points.content: The OFPD is successfully applied in photoplethysmography (PPG) for real-time heart-rate monitoring, detecting a heart rate of 70 beats per minute via light absorption changes in tissue.
knowledge_points.evidence: The device is demonstrated in photoplethysmography for real-time heart-rate monitoring... The heart rate can be determined as 70 beats min^-1 (Figure 4f).
